Morgan — hi, Marissa here. Below is the minimal outbound gate we recommend for a private endpoint deployment (control plane + object store) for the POC. This is intentionally conservative; we can tighten once the NAT/egress path is agreed.

High level
- All outbound traffic from customer VPC to Redwood control plane must be TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3). No plain HTTP required.
- Prefer FQDN-based allowlisting with short TTLs, but understand some customers need IP ranges. We publish both for the POC.

Recommended allowlist (POC) - Control plane API endpoints (TLS):
  - control-plane.redwood-inference.com (SNI host: control-plane.redwood-inference.com)
  - IPs (POC): 23.101.44.128/26, 52.44.130.0/25
- Object storage / artifact uploads (S3-compatible):
  - objects.redwood-inference.com (SNI host: objects.redwood-inference.com)
  - IPs (POC): 34.210.200.0/24
- Telemetry and metrics ingest (HTTPS POST):
  - metrics.redwood-inference.com
  - IPs (POC): 18.205.60.0/24
- Ports/protocols - 443/tcp: required for all outbound traffic to Redwood endpoints (control, object, metrics).
- 53/udp: only if you must resolve external DNS from the VPC (we recommend using VPC Resolver + conditional forwarder).
- 123/udp: optional for NTP if your hosts do not sync internally (we prefer you sync to a local NTP pool).

Connection behavior - Persistent TLS session reuse is used for many clients to reduce latency — expect long-lived outbound TLS sessions from customer subnet to control-plane endpoints.
- We support HTTP/2 multiplexing on control-plane endpoints; make sure intermediate proxies allow HTTP/2 or allow upgrade.

NAT/static IP guidance - For POC: a NAT pool (rotating addresses) is acceptable. For production we recommend either:
  1) Static egress IPs (preferred) — gives stable allowlist and simpler firewall rules.
  2) If using a NAT pool, provide the full CIDR(s) so we can map expected connections — and plan for periodic rotation windows.

TLS inspection and SNI - If BlueSky performs TLS inspection (MITM), we need either:
  - SNI allowed through as control-plane.redwood-inference.com; OR
  - Exception for our endpoints to avoid breaking certificate pinning and token exchange.

Certificates and auth - All API calls use mTLS only when configured; otherwise bearer tokens over TLS are used. We'll share the token exchange endpoints and any client cert requirements once you pick a path (static IPs + mTLS is the most locked-down option).

Attachments: I attached a small diagram for the POC flow and the template Logan sent. If you can tell us whether you can reserve two static egress IPs for the POC we can tighten the list and create the final ACLs.

—Marissa
